environment.description: Same Terraform provider binary running on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement module (terraform_provider_custom_t). The TE module confines the provider process to type terraform_provider_custom_t which has file transition rules allowing write only to objects labeled terraform_provider_custom_conf_t (applied via fcontext to /var/lib/terraform-provider-custom/configs(/.*)?). Additionally, an AppArmor-equivalent restriction is layered via a seccomp-bpf profile attached at systemd unit level (SystemCallFilter=~@raw-io @mount @reboot, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/terraform-provider-custom/configs) that uses ProtectSystem=strict and TemporaryFileSystem=/tmp. The SELinux boolean terraform_provider_network_notify is set to off, denying connect permission to any socket type except unix_dgram_socket for logging. Note: the seccomp profile does NOT filter write() syscall itself - it relies on the SELinux MAC label check to deny writes outside the confined path. The provider CAN still call fmt.Sprintf and process format strings - the control only prevents the file write and network exfiltration stages of the exploit chain.

config.selinux_type_transitions: terraform_provider_custom_t can only write to terraform_provider_custom_conf_t labeled paths
config.path_traversal_blocked_by: SELinux label check - traversed paths outside configs/ have different type labels (default_t, etc_t, etc.) which terraform_provider_custom_t has no write permission to
config.network_exfil_blocked_by: SELinux terraform_provider_network_notify=off denies outbound socket connect
